name: Globe artichoke
grown_as: A hardy perennial vegetable grown for its flower buds; the edible artichoke is the Scolymus Group of Cynara cardunculus (also called Cynara scolymus). Often left to flower for bees.
habit: A big fountain-shaped clump of arching silver-grey leaves about 1 m high and across, with thick, ribbed, upright flower stems to 1.5 m in summer.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the crown, plus a few up the flower stems
leaf.outline: Long, 50 cm to 1 m, cut almost to the midrib into many lobes, which are themselves lobed and toothed; looks like a giant thistle leaf
leaf.base: Narrowed onto a broad flattened stalk
leaf.margin: Lobed and toothed; garden kinds have few or no spines
leaf.veins: A very thick pale midrib, white-felted beneath
leaf.surface: Grey-green above with a fine silvery down, thickly white-woolly beneath

flower.form: A thistle head: a big globe of overlapping scale-like bracts with a dome of many thin tubular florets bursting out of the top
flower.petals: None in the usual sense: hundreds of narrow tubular florets with long thread-like tips
flower.centre: The whole head is florets; no separate centre
flower.behind: Broad, thick, fleshy, overlapping bracts in many rows, green tinged purple, each with a notched or short-pointed tip
flower.carried: One large head at the top of each thick stem, with smaller heads on side branches, all upright
flower.season: July to September; buds cut for eating from June

fruit: After flowering the head dries brown and opens into a mass of silky white plumes (pappus), each carrying a grey-brown, mottled, oblong seed about 6 to 8 mm.
seedling: Two thick, oval seed leaves; the first true leaves simple, oval, toothed and grey-downy, becoming more deeply lobed as the plant grows.
winter: Often keeps a smaller clump of grey leaves in mild winters; in hard winters dies back to the crown. Old flower stems cut down.

leaf: a long leaf cut nearly to the midrib into many toothed lobes
bloom: a dome of violet-blue thread-like florets
rising from a globe of overlapping green-purple bracts
seedling: a simple toothed grey first leaf
young: a fountain of large arching leaves
crop: tight green globe buds of overlapping fleshy bracts on thick upright stems
flower: open violet thistle heads on tall thick stems
heads held above the silver-grey leaves
seedhead: white fluffy plumes bursting from the top
dormant: a low clump of grey leaves or a bare crown

look_alikes: Cardoon is the same species with spinier leaves and smaller, spiny heads. Spear thistle and other thistles are spiny and far smaller. Onopordum (Scotch thistle) has spiny winged stems.
